decision: build the personal agent on OpenClaw
why: most mature self-hosting and security story: MIT, foundation-stewarded, sandboxing, an exposure runbook, and a completed security audit
it is a hosted Meta product, which defeats the point of owning the deployment; a 0-day with a 10.0 CVE is also circulating in the source thread
evidence: Muse Glimmer 30B is Meta's open-weight model; r/better_claw thread comments

why: it is a workflow-enforcement layer, not an agent; it gates another agent's tool calls (Claude-native today)

decision: keep Hermes as the fallback alternative
why: self-improving loop, Python, built-in cron, and a documented migration path from OpenClaw

decision: run on Windows with WSL2 now, and on the homelab Windows 10 + WSL2 later
why: match the homelab target so the artifacts move across unchanged

decision: create openclaw-homelab in simpsonm09-dev from repo-template, fork to simpsonm09, clone under projects/repos
why: matches the fleet workflow in repo-standard governance and the projects folder convention
evidence: gh repo create from template, fork, clone

decision: ship the minimum safe baseline, including tools.exec.security deny
why: the runbook names it the safe starting point; exec is the highest-impact tool

decision: keep config/openclaw.json as strict JSON with a placeholder token
why: lets the standard library validate it and stops a real secret from being committed

decision: stop at documentation and configuration; no install or machine build-out
why: user direction: repo setup and documentation only
